What to photograph — products

The film is built from your stills. Every shot begins and ends on a real photograph of the real product; the camera move between them is the only thing generated. So the stills are the whole job.

The short version

  • One product per folder.
  • Same lighting and same background for every frame. This matters more here than anywhere else: the camera has to travel between two of your photos, and if the light changes between them the move looks like a cut.
  • Originals. No filters, no added shadows, no background swaps.
  • Name the file after the frame: hero.jpg, detail.jpg, scale.jpg.

The three we cannot cut without

  1. Three-quarter beauty shot — Turned slightly off square so two faces show. This is the frame the film opens on.
  2. One close detail — Fill the frame with the stitching, weld, grain or edge you are proud of.
  3. Beside something of known size — Next to a hand, a phone, a coin — anything a buyer already knows the size of.

Two things to know before you send

1. Photographs with people in them. in_use and scale frames often contain a real person. We accept them, but tell us — generating motion across a photograph of an identifiable person is a different legal question from moving a camera past a handbag, and some platforms treat it differently. It is flagged at intake either way.

2. We make no claims. The film shows the product. It will not say it is the best, the fastest or the only one, and it will not carry a testimonial. The FTC rule on consumer reviews and testimonials (in force since October 2024) bans AI-generated testimonials outright — regardless of disclosure — with penalties per violation in the tens of thousands. Product claims are yours to make in the caption, where you can stand behind them.

What makes a frame unusable

  • Different background or lighting from the rest of the set
  • A drop shadow or reflection added in post
  • Heavy retouching — we do not edit your photos, so what you send is what ships
  • Screenshots, or images re-saved from a message thread

What happens next

Send the folder. We check it, flag anything missing within a couple of hours, and deliver the next day.
